newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam aims to increase tonnes milled.
newsitem.headline: Northam aims to increase tonnes milled.

text.p: South Africa's Northam Platinum Ltd said on Thursday it aimed to raise its milling rate and thereby hoped to insure profitability.
"The key to this mine is to get that milling rate up and keep it there," said Peter Janisch, executive director of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd's coal, base metals and platinum operations.
Northam shrank its second quarter pre-capex loss to 0.63 million rand from the first quarter's 18.44 million rand loss.
"We seem to be getting the mining operations right," Janisch said at Gold Fields second quarter results presentation.
But he said that working costs were unfortunately higher than had been hoped. "The costs regrettably have gone a little higher than we would have liked," Janisch said.
Cost of sales for the quarter was 138.38 million rand compared to 131.71 million rand.
Janisch said that Northam had made use of the surge in platinum group metals prices in early June by selling metal they had in stock.
On June 6 the platinum price touched $500 an ounce.
